issues.issue_title: HAL_FLASHEx_OBProgram erases write protection if read protection is also selected
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: HAL_FLASHEx_OBProgram erases write protection if read protection is also selected
Context: repo=stm32f1xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=16
Root cause: Hello @benedekkupper, Thank you for your report, i believe this behavior is correct.
Fix: This is more of a code-review style bug report, so I skip the unnecessary administration.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, bug_report, medium, bug, invalid, flash, HAL_FLASHEx_OBProgram, FLASH_OB_EnableWRP, FLASH_OB_DisableWRP, FLASH_OB_RDP_LevelConfig

Technical details:
This is more of a code-review style bug report, so I skip the unnecessary administration. HAL_FLASHEx_OBProgram calls FLASH_OB_EnableWRP or FLASH_OB_DisableWRP when write protection options are passed into it. Afterwards it calls FLASH_OB_RDP_LevelConfig if read protection options are passed into it. All 3 of these internal methods perform an OB erase, so when write and read protection are both selected, then 1. OB is erased 2. write protection bits are written into OB 3. OB is erased 4. read protection byte is written into OB So the write protection bits aren't applied as intended.

Key comments:
Hello @benedekkupper, Thank you for your report, i believe this behavior is correct. According to the [STM32F10xxx XL-density Flash programming](https://www.st.com/resource/en/programming_manual/pm0068-stm32f10xxx-xldensity-flash-programming-stmicroelectronics.pdf) manuel **page 19** > On every system reset, the option byte loader (OBL) reads the information block and stores > the data into the Option byte register (FLASH_OBR) and the Write protection register > (FLASH_WRPR). Each option byte also has its complement in the information block. > During option loading, by verifying the option bit and its complement, it is possible to check that the > loading has correctly taken place. If this is not the case, an option byte error (OPTERR) is > generated. When a comparison error occurs the corresponding option byte is forced to > 0xFF. The comparator is disabled when the option byte and its complement are both equal > to 0xFF (Electrical Erase state). Please do not hesitate to ask if anything is unclear, and keep me informed BR, Mohamed Chaker. Hello @benedekkupper, I hope you are doing well, please let us know if you encounter any specific unexpected behavior or errors,

issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Unexpected WRP0 Value When Disabling Write Protection on STM32F103C6
Context: repo=stm32f1xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=UART, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=15
Root cause: Hello @xbin-xu, Yes, you are right.
Fix: ## How to enable/disable FLASH WRP > - **Device**: STM32F103C6Tx > - **Firmware Package**: STM32Cube FW_F1 v1.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, UART, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, flash, WRP, FW_F1, GCC, HAL_FLASHEx_OBProgram, WRP0

Technical details:
## How to enable/disable FLASH WRP > - **Device**: STM32F103C6Tx > - **Firmware Package**: STM32Cube FW_F1 v1.8.6 (latest) > - **Toolchain**: GCC When using HAL_FLASHEx_OBProgram() to **disable** write protection (WRP) on specific pages, the resulting Option Byte value is unexpected. ### Code and Log 1. On power-up, all flash pages are **not** write-protected. 2. After enabling WRP on pages 0–31, WRP0 becomes 0x00. 3. After **disabling** WRP on pages 0–3, WRP0 becomes 0xFF(expected 0x01) c void print_option_bytes(void) { __IO uint8_t *ob = (__IO uint8_t *)OB_BASE; __IO uint8_t *ob_end = (__IO uint8_t *)(OB_BASE + 16); printf("ob(%p): ", ob); while (ob < ob_end) { printf("%02x ", *ob++); } printf("\b\r\n"); } void flash_write_wrp(uint8_t wrp_enable, uint32_t wrp) { FLASH_OBProgramInitTypeDef flash_ob; flash_ob.OptionType = OPTIONBYTE_WRP; flash_ob.WRPState = wrp_enable ? OB_WRPSTATE_ENABLE : OB_WRPSTATE_DISABLE; flash_ob.WRPPage = wrp; HAL_FLASH_Unlock(); HAL_FLASH_OB_Unlock(); HAL_StatusTypeDef result = HAL_FLASHEx_OBProgram(&flash_ob); HAL_FLASH_OB_Lock(); HAL_FLASH_Lock(); printf("flash_write_wrp ret: %d\r\n", result); print_option_bytes(); HAL_FLASH_OB_Launch(); } int main(void) { HAL_Init(); SystemClock_Config(); MX_GPIO_Init(); MX_USART2_UART_Init(); // -- User Code printf("system start\r\n"); print_option_bytes(); uint8_t ch = 0; while (1) { if (HAL_UART_Receive(&huart2, &ch, 1, HAL_MAX_DELAY) != HAL_OK) { continue; } printf("\n recv ch: %c(%x)\r\n", ch, ch); if (ch == 'w') { flash_write_wrp(1, OB_WRP_PAGES0TO31MASK); // protect 0~31 } else { flash_write_wrp(0, OB_WRP_PAGES0TO3); // disable 0~3 } } return 0; } txt system start # mcu power on ob(0x1ffff800): a5 5a ff ff ff ff ff ff ff 00 ff ff ff ff ff ff w # pc send 'w' recv ch: w(77) # mcu recv 'w' flash_write_wrp ret: 0 # enable protect 0~31 pages success ob(0x1ffff800): a5 5a ff ff ff ff ff ff 00 ff ff ff ff ff ff ff # ok: wpr0 is 0x00 system start # after HAL_FLASH_OB_Launch ob(0x1ffff800): a5 5a ff ff ff ff ff ff 00 ff ff ff ff ff ff ff W # pc send 'W' recv ch: W(57) # mcu recv 'W' flash_write_wrp ret: 0 # disable protect 0~3 pages success ob(0x1ffff800): a5 5a ff ff ff ff ff ff ff 00 ff ff ff ff ff ff # ?: expected 0x01 system start # after HAL_FLASH_OB_Launch ob(0x1ffff800): a5 5a ff ff ff ff ff ff ff 00 ff ff ff ff ff ff ### Try analysis The following code is FLASH_OB_DisableWRP in STM32F103x6(remove unused code) 1. If WriteProtectPage is 0x01 - WriteProtectPage: will be 0x00 | 0x01 = 0x01 - WRP0_Data: will be 0x01 & 0xFF = 0x01 2. After HAL_FLASHEx_OBErase();: OB->WRP0 is 0xFF, 3. After OB->WRP0 |= WRP0_Data;: is OB->WRP0 is 0xFF | 0x01 = 0xFF Is this a bug in the HAL library or a problem caused by incorrect usage on my part? c static HAL_StatusTypeDef FLASH_OB_DisableWRP(uint32_t WriteProtectPage) { HAL_StatusTypeDef status = HAL_OK; uint16_t WRP0_Data = 0xFFFF; /* Check the parameters */ assert_param(IS_OB_WRP(WriteProtectPage)); /* Get current write protected pages and the new pages to be unprotected ******/ WriteProtectPage = (FLASH_OB_GetWRP() | WriteProtectPage); WRP0_Data = (uint16_t)(WriteProtectPage & OB_WRP_PAGES0TO31MASK); /* Wait for last operation to be completed */ status = FLASH_WaitForLastOperation((uint32_t)FLASH_TIMEOUT_VALUE); if(status == HAL_OK) { /* Clean the error context */ pFlash.ErrorCode = HAL_FLASH_ERROR_NONE; /* To be able to write again option byte, need to perform a option byte erase */ status = HAL_FLASHEx_OBErase(); if (status == HAL_OK) { SET_BIT(FLASH->CR, FLASH_CR_OPTPG); if(WRP0_Data != 0xFFU) { OB->WRP0 |= WRP0_Data; /* Wait for last operation to be completed */ status = FLASH_WaitForLastOperation((uint32_t)FLASH_TIMEOUT_VALUE); } /* if the program operation is completed, disable the OPTPG Bit */ CLEAR_BIT(FLASH->CR, FLASH_CR_OPTPG); } } return status; }

Key comments:
Hello @xbin-xu, Yes, you are right. Thank you for this heads-up. I'll log an internal tracker. BR, Mohamed. ST Internal Reference: 220806 Fixed in commit: c9c90c2e69578405729cfc8f26cdcb9ff49b3522

Problem: Interrupting USB Transfer
Context: repo=stm32f1xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=USB, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=9
Root cause: The 0x3FFU is generating an PMA Overrun wich is resulting in an stalled OUT Endpoint.
Fix: https://github.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, USB, bug_report, medium, bug, invalid, internal bug tracker, STM32F103, OUT, USBD_STATUS_STALL_PID, HAL_PCD_EP_Receive, USB_EPStartXfer

Technical details:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f1xx_hal_driver/blob/ddf259a6eb9dc4ba421f5e2b1ae619bd77468214/Inc/stm32f1xx_hal_pcd.h#L868 This line of code is interrupting my USB Transfer in random time on STM32F103. In Wireshark i see the OUT Endpoint answered with USBD_STATUS_STALL_PID The host is continously sending Data to the OUT Pipe. While debugging the **HAL_PCD_EP_Receive** , until this line of code, the connection is stable. Stepping over it will interrupt the Transaction and on Host the Pipe is broken. In normal running, the next line in Debug, will reactivate the Pipe to valid state, so the host is not recognizing it. But some interrupts occour within this two lines and the transfer is broken. The two lines are part of **USB_EPStartXfer**: - 2441: PCD_SET_EP_RX_CNT(USBx, ep->num, len); - 2467: PCD_SET_EP_RX_STATUS(USBx, ep->num, USB_EP_RX_VALID); After deleting this line, i had no transfer interruptions any more.

Key comments:
The 0x3FFU is generating an PMA Overrun wich is resulting in an stalled OUT Endpoint. The Host is running a WinUSB Driver wich could not handle this Error State. A pipe reset was required to continue the transfer. The STM32F1 is running wihtout any peripherals, just USB and the HSE Oscilator was activated with CubeMX. The USB Part was configured with 1 OUT and 1 IN EP with 64 Byte of maximum packet size for Bulktransfer. The STM32F1 Application was reduced to a while(1) which is coninously calling HAL_PCD_EP_Receive and a short timeout of 1ms to simulate the data handling. The Error happend on different devices. If you need support, just ask. I have saved the example project to reproduce the error. Hi @AndyD87, Thank you very much to propose your support. Problem: Changing the write-only AFIO_MAPR.SWJ_CFG field in LL
Context: repo=stm32f1xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=8
Root cause: Hello @wek3, Thank you for your contribution.
Fix: In stm32f1xx_ll_gpio.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, bug_report, high, bug, st community, LL_GPIO_AF_EnableRemap_SWJ, LL_GPIO_AF_Remap_SWJ_NONJTRST, LL_GPIO_AF_Remap_SWJ_NOJTAG, LL_GPIO_AF_DisableRemap_SWJ, SET_BIT, AFIO, MAPR

Technical details:
In stm32f1xx_ll_gpio.h, LL_GPIO_AF_EnableRemap_SWJ(), LL_GPIO_AF_Remap_SWJ_NONJTRST, LL_GPIO_AF_Remap_SWJ_NOJTAG(), LL_GPIO_AF_DisableRemap_SWJ() all use SET_BIT(AFIO->MAPR, AFIO_MAPR_SWJ_CFG_xxxxx); which is incorrect, as SET_BIT is #define SET_BIT(REG, BIT) ((REG) |= (BIT)) and the read value of AFIO_MAPR.SWJ_CFG field according to RM0008 is unpredictable. This has been reported in https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus-embedded-software/incorrectly-written-afio-mapr-swj-cfg-bits-in-cubef1-ll/m-p/90756 , can you please drop a comment there, too. Thanks, Jan Waclawek

Key comments:
Hello @pi, Thank you for this report. We will get back to you as soon as we analyze it further. This may take some time. Thank you for your comprehension. Rania See also [STM32CubeF4#88](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/issues/88). Hi @pi, Could you please give us more details on how you encountered this issue so that we can better analyze it? Hi @TOUNSTM I found this error while examining the function code. In fact, this error should never occur. Flash remains locked during any operations, so the condition (ProcedureOnGoing != FLASH_PROC_NONE) will never be satisfied. It's just that the eye caught on the potential for a deadlock to occur. Problem: SetPinMode and SetPinPull sequence
Context: repo=stm32f1xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=high, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=3
Root cause: Hi @mgiaco, First, we would like to thank you for your contribution.
Fix: Hello, I switched to the latest cubef1 today.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, usage_question, high, question, LL_GPIO_SetPinMode, GPIO_InitStruct, LL_GPIO_SetPinPull, LL_GPIO_MODE_OUTPUT, LL_GPIO_MODE_ALTERNATE, assert_param, IS_LL_GPIO_SPEED, IS_LL_GPIO_OUTPUT_TYPE

Technical details:
Hello, I switched to the latest cubef1 today. Unfortunately, the device stopped working :-( I then found out that it had to do with these changes (stm32f1xx_ll_gpio.c): old: /* Pin Mode configuration */ LL_GPIO_SetPinMode(GPIOx, currentpin, GPIO_InitStruct->Mode); /* Pull-up Pull-down resistor configuration*/ LL_GPIO_SetPinPull(GPIOx, currentpin, GPIO_InitStruct->Pull); if ((GPIO_InitStruct->Mode == LL_GPIO_MODE_OUTPUT) || (GPIO_InitStruct->Mode == LL_GPIO_MODE_ALTERNATE)) { /* Check speed and Output mode parameters */ assert_param(IS_LL_GPIO_SPEED(GPIO_InitStruct->Speed)); assert_param(IS_LL_GPIO_OUTPUT_TYPE(GPIO_InitStruct->OutputType)); /* Speed mode configuration */ LL_GPIO_SetPinSpeed(GPIOx, currentpin, GPIO_InitStruct->Speed); /* Output mode configuration*/ LL_GPIO_SetPinOutputType(GPIOx, currentpin, GPIO_InitStruct->OutputType); } new: if ((GPIO_InitStruct->Mode == LL_GPIO_MODE_OUTPUT) || (GPIO_InitStruct->Mode == LL_GPIO_MODE_ALTERNATE)) { /* Check speed and Output mode parameters */ assert_param(IS_LL_GPIO_SPEED(GPIO_InitStruct->Speed)); assert_param(IS_LL_GPIO_OUTPUT_TYPE(GPIO_InitStruct->OutputType)); /* Speed mode configuration */ LL_GPIO_SetPinSpeed(GPIOx, currentpin, GPIO_InitStruct->Speed); /* Output mode configuration*/ LL_GPIO_SetPinOutputType(GPIOx, currentpin, GPIO_InitStruct->OutputType); } /* Pull-up Pull-down resistor configuration*/ LL_GPIO_SetPinPull(GPIOx, currentpin, GPIO_InitStruct->Pull); /* Pin Mode configuration */ LL_GPIO_SetPinMode(GPIOx, currentpin, GPIO_InitStruct->Mode); Why was this changed? I didn´t found any issue for that in this repo. So i also found an issue here https://community.st.com/s/global-search/LL_GPIO_Init seems to be a little bit related. Can someone have a look on that? many thanks

Key comments:
Hi @mgiaco, First, we would like to thank you for your contribution. Actually, this change aims to correct the GPIO initialization sequence to avoid unwanted pulse on GPIO Pin’s. Indeed, old configuration sequence 1. Pin Mode configuration 2. Pull-up Pull-down resistor configuration 3. Speed mode configuration 4. Output mode configuration causes unwanted pulse generation when initializing of the GPIO registers leading to an incorrect behavior. This sequence has therefore been corrected to avoid this case. The new sequence is then such as updated in the latest release. 1. Speed mode configuration 2. Output mode configuration 3. Pull-up Pull-down resistor configuration 4. Pin Mode configuration The fix was also mentioned in the [Release Note](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f1xx_hal_driver/blob/master/Release_Notes.html) under **"HAL/LL GPIO driver"** section as following : > Update LL GPIO initialization sequence to avoid unwanted pulse on GPIO Pin’s Hope this has given you a better understanding of the fix. Okay so i have to check what´s wrong with my implementaiont. many thanks
